title: Pass a Few Swiftly-fleeting Years
description: Pass a Few Swiftly-fleeting Years in Tonic Solfa to MELCOMBE, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 2 verses and a piano.
about: Charles Wesley wrote these words. His brother John printed them in A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780), hymn 48.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Long Metre (8.8.8.8), and this page sets them to MELCOMBE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Pass a few swift-ly fleet-ing years, And all that now in bod-ies live Shall quit, like me, the vale of tears, Their right-eous sen-tence to re-ceive.

lines: And all that now in bodies live
Shall quit, like me, the vale of tears,
But all, before they hence remove,
And, O my God, shall I be there?

source: John Wesley, A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788), public domain, as printed in John Wesley's Collection of Hymns (1780); set to MELCOMBE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
